questions: What is the exact definition of "p divides N an even number of times" - does this mean the exponent of p in N's prime factorization is even?
Is 1 considered a valid 400 number since it has zero prime factors, or must a 400 number have exactly two distinct prime factors?
What should be returned if there is no 400 number less than or equal to A in the given range?
How should ties be broken when multiple 400 numbers have the same value (though this seems impossible given the definition)?
Are the prime factors of N required to be distinct, or can they include repeated primes with even exponents?
What is the precise mathematical term for "divides an even number of times" - is this standard terminology?
Should the output format include any specific formatting requirements like trailing spaces or specific line endings?
Is the constraint that A ≥ 36 guaranteed to always allow at least one valid 400 number to exist?

inline_prompts:
A positive integer N is a 400 number if and only if it satisfies both of the following two conditions:
- N has exactly 2 distinct prime factors.
- For each prime factor p of N, the maximum integer k such that p^k divides N is even. In other words, all exponents in the prime factorization of N are even. 
Process Q queries. Each query gives you an integer A, so find the largest 400 number not exceeding A. 
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
Q
\text{query}_1
\text{query}_2
\vdots
\text{query}_Q
Here, \text{query}_i is the i-th query, given in the following format:
A
Output
Print Q lines. The i-th line should contain the answer to the i-th query.
Constraints
- 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5
- For each query, 36 \leq A \leq 10^{12}.
- All input values are integers.
